content:
I would like to add an API for probabilistic computation. I am new to contributing here, and I wanted to ask whether anyone has already explored this problem before or whether there is an expected roadmap for it.

The API I have in mind is similar to the TimeT monad, but with additional methods for extracting random bits/words from a generator. A generator could be either a theoretically perfect random generator or a supplied pseudorandom generator.

I can experiment with the idea in a separate repo before turning it into a pull request. Let me know your thoughts on this.
have you seen mathlib's PMF monad and Giry monad?

Shreyas Srinivas said:

have you seen mathlib's PMF monad and Giry monad?

I think I can definitely use those. I will try to experiment and post any updates here thank you!
I think the earliest formalisation of something resembling PAC learning was from this paper and they designed a Giry monad for this purpose. This was in lean 3 of course.

Hi Christos, yes, we plan to extend TimeM to TimeT to handle randomized algorithms. A preliminary version has been done in the context of quicksort. The idea is to use a typeclass so that one can execute the algorithm, interpret it as a PMF, or use any probability monad.
It would be nice to have TimeT with a random bits generator. Currently, the formalization above just assumes that you have access to an oracle that gives a random index in a list.
If permitted by mods, I can also show you how I add randomness in my approach to algorithms.

Shreyas Srinivas said:

If permitted by mods, I can also show you how I add randomness in my approach to algorithms.

There is no permission to give. Discussing contributions to CSLib is welcome (under the usual CoC). If you're concerned because you think this will make the discussion off topic (e.g., a long discussion not aimed at contributing to CSLib), there's always the general computer science channel.

I have previously been asked not to mention Algolean here, even though the code from Algolean is essentially the free monad model which is in a CSLib PR and it is relevant to the topic at hand. That is why I am checking first.

Basically I implemented a (distribution agnostic) random sample query and some code to take any model and produce its randomised version. Eventually it can be used in CSLib, not only for traditional random algorithms and PAC learning but many other scenarios. OTOH, we also need a distribution-gnostic query model for some models of algorithms which is just one small PR away.

Further the query can also be used for non-deterministic computation, by using it with a different model : one which receives an existentially quantified Prop, and extracts the certificate by Classical.choose
Christos might also be interested in the ProbComp type from VCVio.
